title: Catalan Rigidity of Even Lattice Paths

creators.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
creators.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
A family of North–East lattice paths from (0,0) to (n,n) in which any two paths share an even number of edges has at most 2n members. We prove Shankar's conjecture (arXiv:2607.23117, Conjecture 4.1) that exactly Cn families attain this bound, one for each noncrossing perfect matching, by classifying all equality cases of the underlying inequality: they are the skeleton systems, and there are C(m,⌊m/2⌋) of them. We also compute the binary rank of every grid graph, ab − gcd(a+1,b+1) + 1, give eventown and oddtown bounds for paths in every rectangle, show that the odd families of paths from (0,0) to (n+1,n) of size 2n number at least Cn+1, determine the largest odd family in the n × n square for n ≤ 6 (1, 2, 3, 6, 10, 16) with lower bounds 20 and 28 for n = 7, 8, and construct even and odd families in the a × 2 rectangle of sizes ⌊a/2⌋+3, ⌊(5a−1)/4⌋ and ⌊(5a−2)/4⌋, optimal for a ≤ 22. The growth of the largest odd family in the square, whether 2n bounds the odd families from (0,0) to (n+1,n), and the exact even value in non-square rectangles remain open.

The archive contains the paper (preprintCatalanRigidity: LaTeX source and PNG figures; dist: PDF and tex zip), the maximum clique search and the checks of the two-row families (verification/catalan-rigidity), and the earlier paper on Shankar's conjecture with its checks in C, C++, Bash, Python, Julia and Lean 4.
